The packed V plane (16-lane build) and the native K plane cross the cache and kernel boundaries as typed views. A bare pointer or the other plane's view is a compile error (tested with `STATIC_REQUIRE`).

`native_k_view` is an alias of the generic row-major `view`, and t_llama_unit asserts it is constructible from `const bf16*`. So any pointer or row-major 64x128 bf16 view passes the QK kernel; "a bare pointer is a compile error" holds for V only.

result.consequence_for_rule: Codex's qualification is right and it refines the claim-vs-enforcement rule rather than overturning it. The rule should grade an "X is a compile error" claim on three enforcement levels and name the level the code reaches: (1) direct call with a bare pointer rejected (needs only an explicit constructor; both K and V reach this, tested by amx_qk_accepts/amx_pv_accepts at t_llama_unit.cpp:383-384,388-389); (2) one-line explicit wrap of an arbitrary pointer rejected (needs a private or absent pointer constructor; V reaches this via v_vnni.hpp:137 private ctor and the is_constructible FALSE probes at 394-395; K does NOT, line 397 asserts the wrap is allowed and t_amx_numerics.cpp:165 uses it on a raw fixture array); (3) the parameter type is nominally distinct from any generic view of the same shape (V yes; K no, because const_native_k_view is a `using` alias of the generic const_view, kv_cache_fwd.hpp:49, so any row-major 64x128 bf16 const_view is the same type). Two sub-rules follow. (a) When a test uses std::is_constructible_v, read it as "explicit construction allowed", never as "implicit pass allowed": is_constructible is true for explicit constructors, so line 397 is not evidence that a bare pointer passes at the call. (b) When a PR description says "typed view" or "cannot be handed in by mistake" (amx_attn_iface.hpp:220), check whether the type is a nominal new type or a `using` alias; an alias gives layout-by-shape only, not provenance, and the description must say which. The reply to Wade should concede levels (2) and (3) for K (his substantive point) while correcting the literal wording "any pointer ... passes": a bare pointer at the call is rejected for K as well (line 383), only a pointer wrapped in one explicit line passes.

result.consequence_for_rule: A "duplicate coverage" rule needs the guard "same observation point". Two tests that drive the same code paths (here: all four copy_token parities through book::append) are duplicates only when they assert the same observable at the same point. Executable form: (1) for each test, list the observable it asserts (which memory, which assertion) and the implementation branch that produced that memory at the observed point; (2) for a GENERATE/parametrised test, do this per parameter value (here: dst_tokens 2 -> last copy even<-even -> andnot branch v_vnni.hpp:361-364; dst_tokens 3 -> last copy even<-odd -> srli branch v_vnni.hpp:380-383); (3) check whether a later write in the same test overwrites the observable before the assertion (here: the full-page bit-exact section overwrites every odd partner, so it is blind to partner clearing, and the poison section never compares destination with source, so it is blind to row-copy bit errors); (4) call it duplicate only if the observable sets coincide. Here they are disjoint: the poison GENERATE is the only observation of both partner-clearing branches, and the bit-exact section is the only observation of the row bits. Reducing the poison section to one GENERATE value would drop one clearing branch from observation; dropping the bit-exact section would drop the row-bit check.
result.notes: Decision on the three-way question: both partly, with codex's objection the correct conclusion. Wade's factual premise is right: both sections run all four parities through book::append (verified from copy_storage_slot's dst_begin+i / src_begin+i loop and the GENERATE values 2/3). Wade's conclusion ("one parity here already protects the NaN zeroing, so one of these is duplicate") is wrong on two counts verified at 96a6220ab6: (a) copy_token has two distinct even-destination clearing branches (andnot at :364 for even source, srli at :383 for odd source) and the poison section's two GENERATE values reach one each at the last copy (dst 6 <- src 4, dst 6 <- src 3), so a single value observes only one branch; (b) the bit-exact section fills the full 64-token page (page_size = 64, kv_cache.hpp:1750), its last copy lands on odd token 63, and the odd-destination branches overwrite the whole odd half (ternarylogic A | (B & ~C) masks the destination's odd half out), so no odd partner left by an even-destination copy survives to the check loop at 3689-3698. Codex's three sub-claims ("separate implementation branches", "two poison configurations end with those different branches", "full-page bit-copy case subsequently overwrites odd partner positions", "partial-page poison case observes the final unused odd partner") are each supported by the lines quoted. Read vs inferred: the parity sequence per GENERATE value is inferred by arithmetic from copy_storage_slot's loop (read) and the GENERATE constants (read); the test's own comment at 3294-3297 states the same pairs. One extra observation not in codex's text: the poison section's value check (3368-3378) compares scaled_v with get_v, both reads of the destination, so it does not verify the copied row bits against the source; the bit-exact section is the only row-bit check. That strengthens "disjoint observables" in both directions. Not run: no test was executed (worktree read only, no build); all claims are from reading the code at 96a6220ab6.
